sections.theory:
If R.E=1\Rightarrow both estimators are equally efficient.

For example, in case of normal distribution both sample mean and sample median are unbiased estimators for μ. However Var(\overline{X})=\frac{\sigma^2}{n} and Var(\text{median})=\frac{\pi\sigma^2}{2n}. Now comparing these estimators by relative efficiency criteria as:

R.E=\frac{Var(\overline{X})}{Var(\text{median})}=\frac{\sigma^2/n}{\pi\sigma^2/2n}=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\cdot\frac{2n}{\pi\sigma^2}=\frac{2}{\pi}

=\frac{2}{22/7}=\frac{14}{22}=0.64<1

This implies that \overline{X} is more efficient than median for μ. Thus, an unbiased estimator which has minimum variance is called the best or the most efficient estimator.

Example 6.7

A random sample X_1,X_2,X_3 is drawn from a normal population having mean μ and variance \sigma^2. Let \hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4} and \hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3} are the estimators for μ.

i) Which of the estimators is unbiased?

ii) Show that \hat{\theta}_1 is efficient estimator for μ than \hat{\theta}_2.

Solution:

i) To check unbiasedness, we first consider:

$\hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}$

Take expectation on both sides

E(\hat{\theta}_1)=\frac{1}{4}E[X_1+2X_2+X_3]

=\frac{1}{4}[E(X_1)+2E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{4}[\mu+2\mu+\mu], As all X_i’s have same mean μ

=\frac{4\mu}{4}=\mu Hence \hat{\theta}_1 is unbiased estimator of μ.

Now consider the second estimator:

\hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}.

E(\hat{\theta}_2)=\frac{1}{3}[E(X_1)+E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{3}[\mu+\mu+\mu]

=\frac{3\mu}{3}=\mu Thus, \hat{\theta}_2 is also an unbiased estimator of μ.

(ii) To check the efficiency, we have first compute variances for both estimators.

Var(\hat{\theta}_1)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}\right]

=\frac{1}{16}[Var(X_1)+4Var(X_2)+Var(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{16}[\sigma^2+4\sigma^2+\sigma^2], As X_i’s are drawn from the population having variance \sigma^2.

$=\frac{6\sigma^2}{16}=\frac{3\sigma^2}{8}.$

Similarly Var(\hat{\theta}_2)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}\right]

i) کون سا تخمین کار غیر جانبدار ہے؟

ii) ثابت کریں کہ μ کے لیے \hat{\theta}_1، \hat{\theta}_2 سے زیادہ مؤثر تخمین کار ہے۔

$\hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}$

\hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}.

=\frac{1}{3}[\mu+\mu+\mu]

=\frac{3\mu}{3}=\mu لہٰذا \hat{\theta}_2 بھی μ کا غیر جانبدار تخمین کار ہے۔

له μ منځني او \sigma^2 واریانس لرونکي نورمال نفوس څخه یوه تصادفي نمونه X_1,X_2,X_3 اخیستل کېږي. فرض کړئ \hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4} او \hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3} د μ اټکلوونکي دي.

i) کوم اټکلوونکی بې‌پلوه دی؟

ii) وښایاست چې د μ لپاره \hat{\theta}_1 تر \hat{\theta}_2 موثر اټکلوونکی دی.

حل:

i) د بې‌پلوي د ازمویلو لپاره لومړی په پام کې نیسو:

$\hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}$

دواړو خواوو ته تمه واخلئ

E(\hat{\theta}_1)=\frac{1}{4}E[X_1+2X_2+X_3]

=\frac{1}{4}[E(X_1)+2E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{4}[\mu+2\mu+\mu]، ځکه چې ټول X_i یو شان منځنی μ لري

=\frac{4\mu}{4}=\mu نو \hat{\theta}_1 د μ بې‌پلوه اټکلوونکی دی.

اوس دویم اټکلوونکی په پام کې ونیسئ:

\hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}.

E(\hat{\theta}_2)=\frac{1}{3}[E(X_1)+E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{3}[\mu+\mu+\mu]

=\frac{3\mu}{3}=\mu نو \hat{\theta}_2 هم د μ بې‌پلوه اټکلوونکی دی.

(ii) د موثریت د ازمویلو لپاره باید لومړی د دواړو اټکلوونکو واریانسونه محاسبه کړو.

Var(\hat{\theta}_1)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}\right]

=\frac{1}{16}[Var(X_1)+4Var(X_2)+Var(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{16}[\sigma^2+4\sigma^2+\sigma^2]، ځکه چې X_i له داسې نفوس څخه راایستل شوي چې واریانس یې \sigma^2 دی.

$=\frac{6\sigma^2}{16}=\frac{3\sigma^2}{8}.$

همداراز Var(\hat{\theta}_2)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}\right]

If R.E=1\Rightarrow both estimators are equally efficient.

For example, in case of normal distribution both sample mean and sample median are unbiased estimators for μ. However Var(\overline{X})=\frac{\sigma^2}{n} and Var(\text{median})=\frac{\pi\sigma^2}{2n}. Now comparing these estimators by relative efficiency criteria as:

R.E=\frac{Var(\overline{X})}{Var(\text{median})}=\frac{\sigma^2/n}{\pi\sigma^2/2n}=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\cdot\frac{2n}{\pi\sigma^2}=\frac{2}{\pi}

=\frac{2}{22/7}=\frac{14}{22}=0.64<1

This implies that \overline{X} is more efficient than median for μ. Thus, an unbiased estimator which has minimum variance is called the best or the most efficient estimator.

Example 6.7

A random sample X_1,X_2,X_3 is drawn from a normal population having mean μ and variance \sigma^2. Let \hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4} and \hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3} are the estimators for μ.

i) Which of the estimators is unbiased?

ii) Show that \hat{\theta}_1 is efficient estimator for μ than \hat{\theta}_2.

Solution:

i) To check unbiasedness, we first consider:

$\hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}$

Take expectation on both sides

E(\hat{\theta}_1)=\frac{1}{4}E[X_1+2X_2+X_3]

=\frac{1}{4}[E(X_1)+2E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{4}[\mu+2\mu+\mu], As all X_i’s have same mean μ

=\frac{4\mu}{4}=\mu Hence \hat{\theta}_1 is unbiased estimator of μ.

Now consider the second estimator:

\hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}.

E(\hat{\theta}_2)=\frac{1}{3}[E(X_1)+E(X_2)+E(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{3}[\mu+\mu+\mu]

=\frac{3\mu}{3}=\mu Thus, \hat{\theta}_2 is also an unbiased estimator of μ.

(ii) To check the efficiency, we have first compute variances for both estimators.

Var(\hat{\theta}_1)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}\right]

=\frac{1}{16}[Var(X_1)+4Var(X_2)+Var(X_3)]

=\frac{1}{16}[\sigma^2+4\sigma^2+\sigma^2], As X_i’s are drawn from the population having variance \sigma^2.

$=\frac{6\sigma^2}{16}=\frac{3\sigma^2}{8}.$

Similarly Var(\hat{\theta}_2)=Var\left[\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}\right]
